title: Rebuild my church
hookLine: at San Damiano a crucifix tells Francis to rebuild; he starts with stones

cards: A small church outside the walls of Assisi, and it's falling down. Cracked walls, a sagging roof, a priest too poor to fix any of it. Inside hangs a painted cross, Christ stretched on it with his eyes wide open.
A young man, the son of a rich cloth merchant, comes in to pray, restless, unsure what his life is for. He kneels in front of that cross. And, the early lives of Francis say, the cross speaks.

teach.b: Bonaventure, in his life of Francis, gives the voice from the cross like this: Francis, go and repair my house, which, as you see, is falling into ruin.
Francis took it literally. The roof was falling in, so he would fix the roof. He sold cloth from his father's shop, and a horse, and brought the money to the priest.
The priest, afraid of Francis's father, wouldn't take it, and Francis tossed it onto a windowsill as if it were dust.
With no money to spend, he begged for building stones in the streets of Assisi, where everyone knew him as a merchant's son. Some people mocked him.
He carried stones on his own back, set them with his own hands, and the little church stood again. He went on to repair other chapels the same way.
Only later, Bonaventure writes, did Francis come to see that the words were mainly about the Church itself, the Church Christ bought with his own blood.

Saint Paul says the same about people, writing to a quarreling congregation, in the Douay-Rheims: "you are God's building." The brothers who gathered around Francis would carry his way far beyond Assisi.
But it started with a young man doing the job right in front of him, literally, one stone at a time.

how: The San Damiano cross is kept in the Basilica of Saint Clare in Assisi, and copies of it hang in Franciscan churches and homes; pilgrims pray before it and visit the restored church of San Damiano.

games.q: a voice from a cross tells you: go and repair my house, which is falling into ruin. you're kneeling in a crumbling chapel. what do you do?

games.why: Francis took it literally and rebuilt San Damiano stone by stone; only later did he see the words were about the Church itself.

practice: Find one small broken thing in your life, a loose button, a squeaky hinge, a promise you let slide, one you could actually fix rather than the biggest. Picture the first stone: the needle, the screwdriver, the message.
If you pray, hold the words from the cross: go and repair my house.

wordCard.voice: San Damiano. The crumbling church outside Assisi whose cross spoke to Francis, who repaired it stone by stone before understanding the words meant the whole Church. Today's word.

carryVoice: Your line: start with stones. Big repairs begin with something small. Day eight hundred six, done.
